question: In a 3D bulk-scale rubidium-87 Gross–Pitaevskii model, what happens to same-history vortex loops and to the first detection of new loops after a translating potential brakes and becomes stationary? How closely does the same equation predict axial oscillation frequencies in a separate, measured 87Rb cylindrical box?
prior_access: P12's published dimensionless observations (notably rings at t≈70 and later at U=0.6 with gamma=0.01) and Garratt et al. Figs. 1, 2 and 5 were visible before design. Fig. 2 frequencies are read from published marker centres; none fixes a simulation coefficient. New intervention histories and computed cylinder eigenfrequencies are generated after registering this plan and declared code. Small synthetic checks test the instruments.
independent_unit: Each of three independently drawn smooth phase perturbations is a paired numerical repeat under the same physical setup at each gamma. Arms are run separately from t=0 and must yield identical prefix field hashes within each pair. Earlier frames, loops within one history, the two gammas, and replays/refinements are not independent physical repeats. Each source frequency is a point from one published trap.
inputs: A phase-perturbed condensate (uniform density, no vortex) in a real 3D periodic domain evolves by a local nearest-neighbour Gross–Pitaevskii stencil with an externally prescribed positive Gaussian potential. Its height, speed and times are set before observing the study runs. The zero damping limit is Hamiltonian. Gamma=0.01 is the old P12 sensitivity value for a phenomenological bath at fixed chemical potential, not a measured rubidium sink. The separate static-cylinder calculation has hard walls and regularity at r=0.
measurement: Save work, bath loss, energy, particle norm, signed nonzero phase circulations and middle density sections starting at t=0. Direct dual-lattice loops must be closed, unambiguous and contractible. A resolved loop has RMS radius >=2 ell and all crossed-face centres at V<=0.5 mu. Track only mutual singleton neighbours within 1.5 ell/tau times the sampling interval and radius ratio in [2/3,3/2]. Cohort means eligible at t=120 and continuously linked back to t=116. Report continuous links at t=132,176,224 and newly detected tracks after t=132 with at least three observed frames when counting all confirmed arrivals. Keep unresolved pieces and track endings as observations. For the cylinder, compare the lowest axial-odd, azimuth-independent Bogoliubov frequency with each digitized figure point, report both cell sizes, geometry sensitivity and no fit.
alternatives: Different arrivals with similar cohort retention would distinguish ongoing formation from short-term persistence; ending a track may reflect contraction below resolution, a tangle, or tracking ambiguity. A static-from-t=0 ramp controls the preparation and measurement. Compare gamma=0 and 0.01, spatial, temporal and extent variants, and re-read obstacle masks V<=0.25 and 1 plus four-time-unit sampling. Vary one solver/extent factor at a time. Axial and transverse sound can cross periodic seams. This is a bulk intervention, not a prediction of the experiment's ring lifetimes or apparatus. Use the declared seed 92101 and gamma=0 base grid for the raw-volume illustration regardless of result.
stopping: All planned cases, t=0 through t=224 in the 3D histories with a fixed observation horizon. The ODE integration does not consult detections. In the cylinder solve, maximum 6000 projected imaginary-time iterations per ground state and convergence criterion residual <=1e-10, then compute the lowest positive odd frequency. Save failures, stops and unexecuted conditions.

reference.paper: Garratt et al. Phys. Rev. A 99, 021601(R) (2019), Fig. 2 and Sections II–III. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1810.08195

material.provenance: The paper uses a about 100 a0. Isotope mass from NIST and SI inputs from CODATA. N=1.2(1)e5 was used in Fig. 5, and the neutral atom mass approximates condensate atom inertial mass.

digitization.procedure: Fit log-axis coordinates to all three major ticks. Use leftmost isolated marker and the seven rightmost mutually isolated markers (no frequency residual-based selection). Coordinates are in the cropped raster with y down. Individual frequency error bars are unresolved at this scale; digitization and geometry bounds are reported as sensitivities, not confidence intervals.

preparation.noise: PCG64 independent normal sine/cosine coefficients, perturbation 0.005/sqrt(5), periods (12,12,48) ell; exact unit modulus in exact arithmetic
preparation.obstacle: Positive periodized Gaussian, sigma=2.5 ell per axis, centred at transverse origin, z starts at 30 ell; height half-cosine ramp to 5 mu over t=0..16, moving-arm velocity half-cosine ramp to 0.68c over t=16..40.

protocol.software: C++17/float64 with -O3 -ffp-contract=off, no fast math. Python 3.10 with NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.15.3, and NumPy PCG64 for the initial field.
